notes: The assigned outcome belongs to the Collins et al. (1998) measures, whereas the replication uses CUSTOM, VOLFLEX, MIXFLEX and TTM. Table 4 separates the two studies; its parallel flexibility lists do not establish paired test identities. The assigned UK subgroup regression is not reported: Tables 6 and 7 report pooled international models, not country regressions. No target was assigned using row order, numerical agreement, or conceptual resemblance. The title/DOI match the supplied replication reference; 2005 online publication and 2006 journal pagination are consistent. Rendered PDF pages 7 and 9 were inspected. Original-side fields are unassigned placeholders. Candidate context only: Tables 6 and 7 explicitly give model n = 285 manufacturing-company responses (analytic units, not employees); 474 manufacturers were in the database and 285 had usable responses. No N sum or df derivation was used. Table 1 lists United Kingdom 29 as sample composition, not an analytic N for a country-specific target regression. The source-wide author verdict is positive (pp. 943–944: The results provide further empirical validation to ... the rigid flexibility model.), but it does not establish a verdict for the unmatched assigned test.
